sections.h2: Where and how to pay the Sheriff
sections.html:
Payment happens at the Sheriff's Office inside the courthouse at 100 South Main Street, Greenville, from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. on weekdays. The number is 270-338-3345, and the mailing address is PO Box 227, Greenville, KY 42345.

  • Bills normally go out October 30, and collection opens November 1.
  • Online payment is possible. Telephone payment is not.
  • A drop box behind the courthouse, near the elevator entrance, takes payments outside office hours.
  • Only full payment is accepted, so a part payment doesn't count.

What the property is worth is a separate question for the county Property Valuation Administrator (PVA). Assessed values can change before they become final.

KRS 134.015 sets the order the sheriff posts: a discount first, then the printed amount, then penalties.

Muhlenberg County bill totals by month paid
Month paidResult for the owner
Whole of NovemberSubtract 2 percent
Whole of DecemberPay the printed total
Whole of JanuaryAdd 5 percent
February 1 through April 15Add 21 percent

In any month the sheriff wants the whole bill paid at once. After April 15 the county clerk handles delinquent bills, so a seller with an old unpaid year should call the clerk for the payoff.

sections.h2: What shapes the Muhlenberg County market
sections.html:
The county covers 479 square miles of western Kentucky, 467 of them land. The Green River and Lake Malone are its two main waters. Greenville is the seat, and Central City is the largest community. Coal built the local economy: Kentucky's first commercial coal mine opened here in 1820 along the Green River at Paradise. Surface coal has been stripped out, and what remains lies deep. The north is gentle hill country with river flats, and the south has higher relief, gorges and sandstone outcrops. Lake Malone State Park sits near Dunmor.

Listings therefore range widely, from town lots in Greenville and Central City to ground near the lake and parcels in old mining country. Lake Malone gives some listings a recreation draw, and the river flats and swamp ground along Cypress Creek can mean flood and drainage questions from lenders and insurers. Greenville's courthouse square and Central City's downtown anchor the two town markets, and each has its own feel for buyers. One school system operates under the Muhlenberg County Board of Education, and a single Muhlenberg County High School has served the county since June 2009.

The population estimate for July 2025 is 30,634, which is 1.0% below the 2020 base, and 21.3% of residents are past 65. Home prices are modest, and so are tax bills.

  • 13,640 housing units in 2025, with just 5 building permits that year.
  • Owners occupy 78.8% of homes.
  • The midpoint for an owned house is $127,400.
  • Monthly owner costs are $1,167 with a mortgage and $396 without.
  • Gross rent has a midpoint of $718.
  • Household income has a midpoint of $51,927.

About 88.7% of residents did not move in the prior year. With so few new permits, a buyer here mostly picks among houses that already exist. A receipt showing the year's bill paid is the quickest answer to a buyer's first question about taxes.

Many calls come from heirs. Central City has a convention center with an outdoor pool and spray park, and Muhlenberg County Public Libraries runs the Thistle Cottage Genealogy and History Annex in Greenville, a useful stop for anyone tracing an old deed chain. Workers spend a mean of 27.0 minutes getting to their jobs, and employment rose 6.7% between 2022 and 2023.

The PVA sets value as of January 1. Under KRS 133.120, the owner first meets the PVA or a deputy during the tax roll's 13-day public inspection in May, which KRS 133.045 schedules. An owner who is still unhappy files a written petition at the County Clerk's office, listing the parcel, the reasons and the proposed value, by the workday after inspection ends.

The board can deny a case when the owner won't hand over the value information it requests, so collect sales comparisons, an appraisal or repair estimates early. A filed appeal doesn't postpone the due date, because the bill stays payable on the normal schedule while the case proceeds. A taxpayer who never appears before the county board cannot reach the state Board of Tax Appeals afterward. Tax is paid on the owner's claimed value, with any increase billed later plus interest.

A Greenville or Central City owner aged 65 or more, or totally disabled, may deduct $49,100 from assessed value for 2025 and 2026. The application goes to the Muhlenberg County PVA, and a birth certificate, driver's license or passport proves age. Disability filers renew annually unless they hold a service-connected rating or have been ruled permanently and totally disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems.

Whoever held title on January 1 owes that year's tax personally. A delinquent bill places a lien on the parcel for up to eleven years under KRS 134.420, regardless of owner.

  • Find out from the sheriff if the current bill is paid, and when.
  • Write the split of the year's tax into the sales contract.
  • Put the buyer's mailing address for future bills on the deed, which KRS 382.135 requires.
  • When a deceased owner's heirs sell, the executor first files an affidavit with the county clerk naming recipients and values.

If the bill is already at the clerk, ask for a payoff dated near closing, since interest and fees keep building. A cash sale as-is lets an heir skip repairs and showings, and the tax is settled from the proceeds at the table.

sections.h2: Coal country and what buyers ask
sections.html:
Buyers ask about jobs, schools and commuting. Coal made this county one of the biggest producers in the country during most of the 1970s, and mining in the county and its neighbors began to grow again as the 2000s opened. The Greater Muhlenberg Chamber of Commerce formed in January 2006 when the Central City and Greenville chambers merged. Schools consolidated in steps, from eight secondary schools to two high schools in 1990 and then to one.

Land near Cypress Creek has bald cypress swamps, and the southern gorges and sandstone outcrops can affect access and building sites. A buyer may ask what is underground on an old mining parcel, so tell them what you know and point them to the PVA and clerk records. The county lies at the southern edge of the Evansville, Indiana television market, which is where many listings get advertised.

Begin at the sheriff's counter and confirm the current bill is paid. Hold on to the receipt. After April 15, call the clerk for the payoff on any delinquent year. Next, call the PVA to confirm the parcel details and any homestead claim on file. Put the tax split in the sales contract, hand the closing agent a written payoff, and record the deed with the buyer's mailing address for future bills.

Heirs should gather the documents that prove who may sign before listing, because the affidavit with the clerk comes first. When a house needs work, a cash buyer who takes it as-is can close on a schedule that fits the payoff, and the seller skips repair bills and open houses.

faqs.q: Is telephone payment accepted by the Muhlenberg County Sheriff?
faqs.a: No. Payment can be made online, mailed to PO Box 227, carried to 100 South Main Street, or left in the courthouse drop box.

faqs.q: May an owner send part of a Muhlenberg County bill?
faqs.a: No. The sheriff requires payment in full.

faqs.q: How long is the Muhlenberg County discount window?
faqs.a: All of November. The printed amount is due in December, and the penalty starts January 1.

faqs.q: What hours does the Muhlenberg County Sheriff keep?
faqs.a: The courthouse counter in Greenville is open weekdays, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. Call 270-338-3345.

faqs.q: What is the Muhlenberg County deduction for seniors?
faqs.a: Once a 65-year-old or totally disabled owner applies at the PVA, $49,100 is taken off assessed value for 2025 and 2026.
